2_Introduction: This work arises from meticulous parameter optimization, where a perovskite solar device was fabricated, reflecting a PCE of 23.6784%, with an FF of 79.9165%, Voc of 1.1844 V, and Jsc of 25.016 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 perovskite precursor (1.65 mol/L) was spin-coated onto the substrate. The perovskite was deposited via a two-step spin-coating procedure, first at 1000 rpm for 5 s and finally at 5500 rpm for 30 s. Antisolvent (150 µL) was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. Subsequent thermal treatment was carried out at 110 °C for 15 min to finalize the perovskite crystal structure.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant A-site cation, supplemented by small amounts of cesium (Cs⁺) and methylammonium (MA⁺) to fine-tune the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.985) and mitigate lattice strain, while the stoichiometric PbI₃.₀ framework ensures optimal charge-carrier effective masses and a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.53 eV; its crystallization kinetics are precisely governed by the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) spreading establishes uniform precursor wetting and early nucleation sites, whereas the high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) phase drives rapid solvent evaporation and supersaturation, with antisolvent dripping (150 µL chlorobenzene) timed at 15 s before spin termination to trigger instantaneous, homogeneous nucleation across the film without premature aggregation, thereby suppressing pinholes and interfacial voids; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min completes crystal maturation by facilitating iodide redistribution, eliminating residual δ-phase impurities, and relieving microstrain—as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of PbI₂ (12.6°) and sharp, narrow (110) and (220) peaks with minimal FWHM—while optical and PL mapping reveal spatially uniform grayscale intensity and >3.2× enhancement in integrated photoluminescence intensity alongside a biexponential decay with dominant long-lived component (τ₁ ≈ 385 ns), confirming drastic suppression of non-radiative recombination centers and homogeneous carrier diffusion across millimeter-scale domains; this morphological and optoelectronic uniformity directly translates into reduced trap-assisted recombination at grain boundaries and interfaces, enabling efficient charge extraction and minimal voltage losses, culminating in a Voc of 1.1844 V, Jsc of 25.016 mA/cm², FF of 79.9165%, and PCE of 23.6784%.
